question: A company needs to copy data from Salesforce CRM to Azure SQL Database every 6 hours for reporting. Which Azure service should they use?
options: Azure Data Factory
Azure Stream Analytics
Azure Synapse Analytics
Power BI
explanation: Scheduled SaaS copies are Data Factory's home turf.

question: A company needs to transform data using Spark with Delta Lake for schema enforcement and evolution. Which Azure service should they use?
options: Azure Data Factory
Azure Databricks
Azure Stream Analytics
Power BI
explanation: Spark plus Delta Lake is Databricks territory.

question: A business wants to analyze clickstream data from website visitors in real-time to personalize user experience. Which Azure service should they use?
options: Azure Synapse Analytics
Power BI
Azure Data Factory
Azure Stream Analytics
explanation: Real-time clickstream personalization is Stream Analytics work.

question: A company needs to load data from REST API with pagination support to Azure SQL Database daily. Which Azure service should they use?
options: Azure Databricks
Power BI
Azure Data Factory
Azure Stream Analytics
explanation: Paginated REST loads on a schedule are Data Factory work.

question: A business wants to run complex ETL pipelines that transform data before loading into data warehouse. Which Azure service should they use?
options: Azure Data Factory
Power BI
Azure Stream Analytics
Azure SQL Database
explanation: Complex transform-before-load pipelines are Data Factory's core job.

question: Match each workload to its service: on-premises ETL to Data Lake, real-time IoT with sub-second latency, collaborative Spark notebooks for ML, unified querying across SQL/Lake/Cosmos. Which mapping is correct?
options: ETL to Stream Analytics, IoT to Databricks, notebooks to Synapse, unified to Data Factory
ETL to Databricks, IoT to Synapse, notebooks to Data Factory, unified to Stream Analytics
ETL to Synapse, IoT to Data Factory, notebooks to Stream Analytics, unified to Databricks
ETL to Data Factory, IoT to Stream Analytics, notebooks to Databricks, unified to Synapse
explanation: Factory moves data, Stream Analytics handles live IoT, Databricks hosts Spark notebooks, Synapse unifies queries. (Interactive dashboards would need Power BI, which is deliberately not among these options.)

question: Match each function to its Synapse component: T-SQL on the lake without infrastructure, MPP warehousing, Spark jobs, pay-per-query, materialized views. Which mapping is correct?
options: Lake queries to Spark, MPP to Serverless, Spark to Dedicated, pay-per-query to Spark, views to Serverless
Lake queries to Serverless, MPP to Spark, Spark to Serverless, pay-per-query to Dedicated, views to Dedicated
Lake queries to Serverless, MPP to Dedicated, Spark to Spark pool, pay-per-query to Serverless, views to Dedicated
Lake queries to Dedicated, MPP to Spark, Spark to Serverless, pay-per-query to Dedicated, views to Spark
explanation: Serverless queries the lake pay-per-query; Dedicated warehouses with MPP and materialized views; Spark pool runs Spark.

question: Match each purpose to its Data Factory component: connection info, structure plus location, orchestrated activities, SQL Database reference, control plus data flow. Which mapping is correct?
options: Connections to Linked Service, structure to Dataset, orchestration to Dataset, SQL ref to Pipeline, flows to Pipeline
Connections to Linked Service, structure to Dataset, orchestration to Pipeline, SQL ref to Linked Service, flows to Pipeline
Connections to Pipeline, structure to Linked Service, orchestration to Dataset, SQL ref to Dataset, flows to Linked Service
Connections to Dataset, structure to Pipeline, orchestration to Linked Service, SQL ref to Pipeline, flows to Dataset
explanation: Linked services connect, datasets describe structure and location, pipelines orchestrate.

question: Match each scenario to its window: hourly non-overlapping aggregates, sessions ending after inactivity, 5-minute moving average, hourly billing counts, variable customer sessions. Which mapping is correct?
options: Hourly to Tumbling, inactivity to Session, average to Sliding, billing to Tumbling, variable to Session
Hourly to Sliding, inactivity to Tumbling, average to Session, billing to Session, variable to Tumbling
Hourly to Session, inactivity to Sliding, average to Tumbling, billing to Sliding, variable to Sliding
Hourly to Tumbling, inactivity to Session, average to Session, billing to Tumbling, billing to Tumbling
explanation: Fixed hourly counts are tumbling, inactivity-bounded activity is session, moving averages slide.

question: Match each description to its Power BI component: single-page canvas, multi-page interactive view, imported data collection, drill-through pages, streaming tiles. Which mapping is correct?
options: Canvas to Report, multi-page to Dashboard, collection to Report, drill-through to Dataset, tiles to Report
Canvas to Dataset, multi-page to Report, collection to Dashboard, drill-through to Dashboard, tiles to Dataset
Canvas to Dashboard, multi-page to Dataset, collection to Dataset, drill-through to Report, tiles to Report
Canvas to Dashboard, multi-page to Report, collection to Dataset, drill-through to Report, tiles to Dashboard
explanation: Single-page canvases and live tiles are dashboards; multi-page drill-through views are reports; collections are datasets.

question: Match each use case to its storage: native-format raw for Spark and SQL, transactional ACID workloads, hierarchical folders, operational T-SQL apps, batch plus real-time source. Which mapping is correct?
options: Raw to ADLS Gen2, transactional to ADLS Gen2, folders to SQL Database, T-SQL apps to SQL Database, dual source to ADLS Gen2
Raw to SQL Database, transactional to SQL Database, folders to ADLS Gen2, T-SQL apps to ADLS Gen2, dual source to SQL Database
Raw to ADLS Gen2, transactional to SQL Database, folders to ADLS Gen2, T-SQL apps to SQL Database, dual source to ADLS Gen2
Raw to SQL Database, transactional to ADLS Gen2, folders to SQL Database, T-SQL apps to ADLS Gen2, dual source to SQL Database
explanation: Raw, hierarchical and dual-purpose analytic storage is ADLS Gen2; transactional and operational T-SQL is SQL Database.

question: Match each benefit to its feature: analyze Cosmos DB without movement, auto RU/s adjustment, lake queries without infrastructure, ACID Spark with schema enforcement. Which mapping is correct?
options: No-movement to Synapse Link, RU/s to Delta Lake, lake queries to Auto-scale, ACID Spark to Serverless
No-movement to Synapse Link, RU/s to Auto-scale, lake queries to Serverless, ACID Spark to Delta Lake
No-movement to Auto-scale, RU/s to Delta Lake, lake queries to Synapse Link, ACID Spark to Serverless
No-movement to Delta Lake, RU/s to Serverless, lake queries to Auto-scale, ACID Spark to Synapse Link
explanation: Synapse Link avoids movement, auto-scale adjusts RU/s, serverless queries the lake, Delta Lake brings ACID to Spark.

question: Match each window to its time behavior: fixed non-overlapping periods, overlapping slide intervals, activity-based dynamic periods, sliding's other name, exactly-one-window events. Which mapping is correct?
options: Fixed to Tumbling, overlapping to Sliding, dynamic to Session, other-name to Hopping, exactly-one to Tumbling
Fixed to Sliding, overlapping to Session, dynamic to Tumbling, other-name to Tumbling, exactly-one to Sliding
Fixed to Session, overlapping to Tumbling, dynamic to Sliding, other-name to Sliding, exactly-one to Session
Fixed to Tumbling, overlapping to Session, dynamic to Session, exactly-one to Hopping, latest to Tumbling
explanation: Tumbling is fixed and exclusive, sliding overlaps, session follows activity, hopping is sliding's alias.

question: Match each ML scenario to its service: Spark MLlib classification, pre-trained models on streams, regression forecasting, fraud detection on IoT, notebooks for features. Which mapping is correct?
options: MLlib to Stream+ML, streams to Databricks, regression to Stream+ML, fraud to Databricks, notebooks to Stream+ML
MLlib to Databricks, streams to Databricks, regression to Stream+ML, fraud to Stream+ML, notebooks to Stream+ML
MLlib to Stream+ML, streams to Stream+ML, regression to Databricks, fraud to Databricks, notebooks to Databricks
MLlib to Databricks, streams to Stream+ML, regression to Databricks, fraud to Stream+ML, notebooks to Databricks
explanation: Spark MLlib training is Databricks; live scoring with Azure ML is Stream Analytics.

question: Match each approach to its tool: visual drag-and-drop, Spark code in Python/Scala, T-SQL in dedicated and serverless pools, Delta Lake ETL. Which mapping is correct?
options: Visual to Synapse, Spark to Data Factory, T-SQL to Databricks, Delta ETL to Power BI
Visual to Data Factory, Spark to Databricks, T-SQL to Data Factory, Delta ETL to Databricks
Visual to Data Factory, Spark to Databricks, T-SQL to Synapse pools, Delta ETL to Databricks
Visual to Databricks, Spark to Synapse, T-SQL to Data Factory, Delta ETL to Stream Analytics
explanation: Visual flows are Data Factory, Spark code is Databricks, T-SQL is Synapse pools, Delta ETL is Databricks.

question: Match each capability to its service: millions of events with millisecond latency, live updating dashboards, reference-data joins, streaming tiles, batch plus streaming together. Which mapping is correct?
options: Volume to Stream, live dashboards to Power BI, joins to Power BI, tiles to Stream, unified to Stream
Volume to Stream, live dashboards to Power BI, joins to Stream, tiles to Power BI, unified to Synapse
Volume to Power BI, live dashboards to Stream, joins to Synapse, tiles to Synapse, unified to Stream
Volume to Synapse, live dashboards to Synapse, joins to Power BI, tiles to Power BI, unified to Power BI
explanation: Stream handles volume and joins, Power BI shows live dashboards and tiles, Synapse unifies batch and stream.
